summary: Added versioned customer, supplier, item, warehouse, lead, project, task and timesheet CRUD with current company/role checks, unique codes, reference guards, audit events and a browser workbench.

Replaced reset-on-restart memory with bounded validated SQLite transactions, rollback on rejected operations, independent-process serialization, random expiring hashed sessions and exclusive setup with generated credentials.

Fixed partial submissions, identical ledger-line loss, insufficient/reserved stock acceptance, zero-rate handling, accepted invoice cost snapshots, payment reference and overpayment checks, linked document policies, quotation replay, report filtering and entity access.

Added retained/exportable drafts, conflict handling, scoped reference selectors, responsive forms, nine detailed learning chapters, original workflow regressions, persistence/failure/process checks and reviewed browser screenshots.

checks.environment: Node 22.16.0, Fastify 5.8.2, TypeScript 5.9.3, Zod 3.25.76, Vitest 3.2.4, builtin SQLite; Chromium 148 in disposable profiles
checks.command: npm.cmd run build; npm.cmd test -- --hookTimeout=60000 --testTimeout=90000; python scripts/verify_browser.py

limits: Local loopback teaching application with a synchronous JSON aggregate in SQLite, 20 MiB workspace, 10000 records per collection and 1000 sessions; not normalized or horizontally scaled storage.

Illustrative USD accounting with whole stock units, purchase rates on receipts and accepted standard costs on sales; no valuation variance reconciliation, taxes, period closing, real payments, bank integration or statutory accounting certification. Stock adjustments are not a complete accounting journal.

Linked documents require complete matching quantities and rates; no partial fulfillment, reversals, manufacturing or reconciliation workflows. Submitted-document replay is supported; durable create-request idempotency is not.

No account provisioning UI, password recovery, MFA, refresh rotation, distributed rate limits or public deployment. Browser focuses on master and project CRUD; operational posting remains API workflows. Inactive-party policy is a documented extension exercise.
Drafts and tokens remain in tab memory; exports are for manual review, not automatic restoration. No all-browser, full accessibility, power-loss or production certification.
